title: Rapidly Deployable Intrusion Detection
metaDescription: Thermal and CCD assessment with buried, fence-mounted, microwave, and taut-wire detection, deployed interim or permanent and configured to site requirements.
heroDek: Detection that has to wait for a permanent design phase isn't protecting anything in the meantime. GSS fields intrusion detection fast, then holds it to a permanent standard.
contextHeading: The gap between the vulnerability and the fix is where risk lives
contextParagraphs: A vulnerability identified in an assessment, a construction laydown area, a temporary boundary, a system down for maintenance. Each creates a window where detection coverage doesn't match the site's actual risk. That window is usually closed with a compensatory measure, and the quality of that measure is rarely questioned the way a permanent system's design is.

GSS treats rapidly deployable IDS as an engineered system, not a stopgap. Detection technology is matched to the terrain and the threat, with buried line sensors and fence-mounted sensors for the perimeter itself, microwave and taut-wire for open ground and constrained approaches, thermal and CCD cameras for assessment once an alarm activates. The combination is selected for the site, not issued from a standard kit.

The same systems that go in fast can stay in permanently, up to and including PIDAS-capable configurations, or come down cleanly once the underlying condition is resolved. Either way, the detection probability and nuisance-alarm rate are documented against the regulatory requirement the deployment is standing in for.

faq.q: How fast can an interim detection system actually be fielded?
faq.a: Timelines are set by the specific gap and terrain rather than a fixed number, but the systems are selected and pre-configured specifically to compress the design-to-commissioning cycle for an interim need.

faq.q: Is an interim system held to a lower detection standard than a permanent one?
faq.a: No. Detection probability and nuisance-alarm rate are validated against the same regulatory requirement the deployment exists to satisfy, whether it stays in for a week or becomes permanent.

faq.q: Can this scale up to a full PIDAS-capable perimeter?
faq.a: Yes. The same technology set and design approach support a PIDAS-capable configuration when the site requires isolation-zone detection rather than a single sensor line.
